channel.name: Fix-It Forest
channel.tagline: Little repairs, one at a time.
channel.description:
In a hollow stump at the edge of the birch wood, Mango the fox runs a very small repair shop.

Every episode, a friend brings her one broken thing — a wobbly stool, a kite that will not fly, a music box that plays too slowly. Mango works out what went wrong, fixes it, and names the idea that made it work, in words a small child can repeat.

Gentle, unhurried stories about noticing, mending, and putting things right. Made for preschoolers and the grown-ups watching with them.

New repair every day.
channel.naming_notes: Channel is named for the format and setting, not the character, so the cast can widen without a rename. 'Mango' was deliberately kept out of the channel name — the Mango Kids namespace already has several established channels and competing there for search would repeat the nursery-rhyme mistake.

series.title: Fix-It Forest
series.logline: In a hollow stump at the edge of the birch wood, a small fox named Mango fixes one broken thing for one forest friend, every day.
series.why_this_survives_policy: One authored property with a fixed cast, a fixed visual style and a fixed 5-beat structure. Every episode is a genuinely different repair with a different physical principle, produced against a dedupe gate. That is the opposite of near-duplicate mass production — the standard YouTube's inauthentic-content policy actually enforces.
series.runtime_rationale: Measured median for character-led kids Shorts was 36s (docs/measured/niche-scan-2026-09-15.md).
series.made_for_kids_rationale: Content is child-directed — a talking animal fixing toys for a preschool audience. COPPA requires the label; mislabelling risks ~$53k/violation. Accept the ~$1-3 RPM and treat Shorts as the discovery engine per the research doc §2.1.

mango.look: rust-orange fur, cream chest, one ear permanently folded at the tip, wears a slightly-too-big canvas apron with four pockets
mango.personality: calm, curious, never panics, narrates what she notices rather than what she feels
mango.voice: warm, unhurried, mid-register, slight smile in the tone
mango.never: never shouts, never uses sarcasm, never fails in a way that scares the owner of the object

bramble.look: dusty brown, wears round glasses too big for his face
bramble.function: brings the broken object about 1 episode in 4; worries out loud so Mango can reassure

world.setting: a hollow stump workshop at the edge of a birch wood, lit by one round window
world.time_of_day: always warm late afternoon — keeps lighting consistent across episodes

visual_style.medium: 2D storybook gouache, visible paper grain, soft edges
visual_style.line: no hard outlines; forms defined by colour blocks and shadow
visual_style.camera: locked-off mid shots and one close-up on the hands at the fix moment
visual_style.text_on_screen: one short caption per beat, bottom third, never covering hands
visual_style.consistency_rule: Every generation prompt must include the cast look block verbatim plus the palette. Character drift across episodes is the single most visible sign of machine production.

episode_formula.engine: One friend brings one broken object. Mango notices one specific cause. She fixes it using one named physical principle. The owner is delighted. The principle is stated once, plainly.
episode_formula.why_it_scales: The broken object, the cause, the principle and the owner are four independent axes. They generate a very large space of genuinely distinct episodes — unlike a template that swaps only a noun.

beats.name: arrival
beats.content: Friend arrives holding the broken thing. We see clearly what is wrong.

beats.name: notice
beats.content: Mango turns it over and names the actual cause out loud. Close on the fault.

beats.name: fix
beats.content: The repair, shown as process. Hands, tools, one clear physical principle at work. This is the retention beat — it must be satisfying to watch.

beats.name: test
beats.content: The object is tested and works. Small, real delight from the owner.

beats.name: name-it
beats.content: Mango names the principle in one short sentence a 4-year-old can repeat.

hard_rules: Never a villain, never a character who broke the object on purpose, never blame.
The fix must be physically real. A child watching must not learn something false.
Never depict a repair a child could copy dangerously — no blades, heat, electricity, small swallowable magnets, or climbing.
One principle per episode, named in plain words, never jargon.
No brand names, no real-world product lookalikes.
Mango never speaks to the camera about subscribing, liking or following.

dedupe_axes.comment: Every episode must differ from recent ones on these axes. Enforced by pipeline/lib/registry.mjs, not by trusting the model.

cause.note: the reason it broke must vary

dedupe_axes.similarity_note: Combined trigram+token similarity against every prior premise. Above this, the episode is rejected and regenerated.
